A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same protein-structure tokenization work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable. Retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering, including v1 Appendix A.3 becoming v2 Appendix A.4.

before.justification: v1 reports original protein reconstruction and generation experiments in Tables 1–2, with sampling and generation analyses in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 reports reconstruction and generation experiments, additional CASP-15 evaluations, reconstruction distributions and a ProteinMPNN likelihood analysis.

M1.justification: The MPNN encoder, masked resampling, FSQ quantizer, AlphaFold structure decoder and GPT prior are retained. Expanded Algorithm 2 details attention computations and positional query initialization already described in v1; it does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds CASP-15 protein reconstruction evaluation in Table 1 and associated figures. This extends benchmark coverage within the existing reconstruction task; PDB training, the CATH novelty reference and protein generation tasks remain.

E2.justification: Figure 22 adds an analytical uniform-random amino-acid reference, -log(1/20), to the new likelihood comparison. Table 1 retains the unquantized autoencoder controls, and Table 2 retains FrameDiff and RFDiffusion. Newly discussed related methods are not added as experimental competitors.

E3.justification: Section 2.2 changes the stated split unit from protein structures to sequence-similarity clusters, materially revising the generalization protocol without establishing that experiments were rerun. v2 also evaluates 432- and 1728-code configurations, introduces CASP-15 median reporting and ProteinMPNN likelihood evaluation, and revises compression accounting.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands reconstruction sensitivity and error analysis through smaller codebooks and per-protein distributions across codebook sizes and downsampling ratios (Figures 2 and 6–17). Figure 22 additionally examines ProteinMPNN likelihood against generated sequence length. The earlier temperature, designability and novelty analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 22 explicitly reports mean ± SEM, while Table 1 introduces median summaries for CASP-15. v1 already contains error bars in generation plots, but does not identify them as SEM. No increase in repeated training runs or new seed information is documented.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises all six quantized reconstruction result pairs; for example, 64000 codes at downsampling 1 changes from 1.59 Å/0.95 to 1.22 Å/0.96. It adds smaller-codebook results and CASP-15 scores, including 0.94 Å/0.97 for that configuration. New distribution and likelihood results also appear. These are revised reports, not established same-setting gains given the changed split description. Table 2 is unchanged.

T1.justification: Table 1 introduces log2(codebook size) into the compression definition and makes reported factors codebook-dependent. This is a limited mathematical-definition revision, although Appendix A.2 Equation 5 still uses fixed 16-bit codes and gives 48r, leaving an inconsistency. The central encoder, quantization and loss equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction objectives and conclusion retain the same contributions: discrete structural representations with high reconstruction fidelity, compression, and a GPT demonstration generating diverse, designable structures. Additional evaluations support these existing claims without redefining their headline scope.

C2.justification: The compression–fidelity explanation, FSQ/codebook-collapse rationale, novelty–designability caveats and acknowledged performance gap to RFDiffusion are retained. The added distribution observations do not introduce a substantive new mechanism explanation or applicability limitation.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the redacted code-access footnote with an explicit repository address, specifies that decoder parameters are learned from scratch, and expands resampling pseudocode with dimensions, initialization and attention operations. Most preprocessing, optimization, hardware and GPT training details are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4 substantially expands positioning around structural tokenization and multimodal generation, including FoldToken/FoldToken2, ProstT5, ProSST, ProTokens, Bio2Token and DPLM-2. It explicitly distinguishes structural-only FSQ tokenization and complete-structure generation from joint sequence–structure approaches and other applications. Existing Foldseek discussion is partly relocated from the introduction.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in related work and additional method explanations. v2 inserts an autoencoding-results appendix subsection, renumbers the retained generation appendix, revises author formatting and citation style, and removes the acknowledgment. Most main-text prose and the conclusion remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 is substantially expanded with additional configurations and CASP-15 columns. New boxplots, reconstruction histograms and the likelihood plot broaden the visual presentation, while retained figures are renumbered and redistributed. The document template and table-caption placement also change. Figures 8–9 introduce caption inconsistencies: captions specify 4096 codes while plot titles specify 64000.

improvement.justification: The additional CASP-15 evaluation and error distributions make reconstruction performance more assessable, while expanded related work, pseudocode and an explicit code address improve positioning and reproducibility information. These gains are limited by incomplete documentation of the added benchmark and inconsistent updating: Section 3.1 still quotes the old Table 1 scores, the compression definition conflicts with Equation 5, and some new captions misidentify configurations. The net improvement is useful but limited.
